thread.title: Tim Cook and Brazil’s president sit together at Davos — despite Bolsonaro’s homophobic remarks

author: Maria LaMagna
title: Tim Cook and Brazil’s president sit together at Davos — despite Bolsonaro’s homophobic remarks
text:
Davos is creating some strange table-mates.
Several Twitter users expressed surprise to see photos of two powerbrokers breaking bread together at the World Economic Forum: Apple CEO Tim Cook AAPL, +0.40% and Brazilian President Jair Bolsonaro. Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella MSFT, +0.97% was also seated at the same table, across from the pair.
Tim Cook, Apple CEO, happily dining with Brazilian fascist President Jair Bolsonaro. pic.twitter.com/wzao7sSbzQ
— Eoin Higgins (@EoinHiggins_) January 23, 2019 There’s a big reason Cook and Bolsonaro don’t seem to be likely dining companions.
Cook is openly gay , and has supported efforts to increase inclusion of LGBTQ people .
Bolsonaro, on the other hand, has gone so far as to suggest children should be beaten to prevent them from “turning gay.” He has also said if he had a gay son, he would be “incapable of loving” him .
He also made disrespectful remarks toward women, including once telling a Brazilian congresswoman, “ I would never rape you because you don’t deserve it.”
He was elected in 2018.
It’s unclear whether the CEOs chose to sit at Bolsonaro’s table. Apple did not immediately return MarketWatch’s request for comment.
But several commentators have said it wasn’t a good choice.
“Really bad optics to sit with a man who preaches violence and has stated that Pinochet didn’t go far enough ,” tweeted Ruth Ben-Ghiat, a columnist . “This pic won’t age well, trust me.” Augusto Pinochet took over power in Chile in the 1970s and 1980s, with U.S. backing, after a military coup. His regime pushed hundreds of thousands of Chileans into exile and is known to have executed thousands of dissidents.
Criticism came from commentators both from Brazil and outside. Many Brazilians expressed concern when Bolsonaro was elected, because of his comments in the past.
“It must have been an interesting table,” said Leon Martins, a Brazilian YouTuber.
“Satya Nadella, Indian immigrant and CEO of Microsoft, and Tim Cook, CEO of Apple who stated “being gay is the best gift God has given me ,” dined with Jair Bolsonaro in Davos,” tweeted Alexandre Aragão, a journalist in Brazil.
Satya Nadella, imigrante indiano e CEO da Microsoft, e Tim Cook, CEO da Apple que afirmou que "ser gay é o melhor presente que Deus me deu", jantaram com Bolsonaro em Davos. https://t.co/WX7AkBFDlv
— Alexandre Aragão (@araga0) January 23, 2019 “How is it possible that @Tim-Cook is having dinner with Jair Bolsonaro, in Davos? A man who once claimed that if he had a gay son he would be unable to love him and he would’ve preferred that he died in an accident,” said Eduardo Arcos , a podcaster from Spain.
“More proof @Tim-Cook’s awful political activism” only applies to the U.S., said Eli Schiff, a design critic.
More proof @tim_cook ’s awful political activism only applies to 🇺🇸 https://t.co/a8O0ga5zYd
— Eli Schiff (@eli_schiff) January 23, 2019 Brazil is a large market for Apple , especially given its status as an emerging market where consumers may increasingly have wealth, as the publication Apple Insider pointed out.
Apple has already said sales were softer than usual for its products in December , which it said is partly because of a slowdown in purchases from China.
